Mukesh Kumar & Anr. Vs. Fso
 Judgment

1. Vide this judgment, I propose to dispose of the present appeal filed by the appellants against the impugned order dated 20.02.2021, whereby the Ld. Adjudicating Officer/Additional District Magistrate (West), Delhi imposed a penalty of Rs.50,000/ u/s 52 of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 (in short "the FSS Act") upon appellant No. 2.
2.

The facts in brief are that on 13.10.2016, Sh. Bal Mukund, Food Safety Officer took a sample of 'Pan Masala' for analysis from Sh. Pawan Kumar Madan S/o Late Sh. Krishan Lal, M/s Pawan Store,
2632/30, Shadi Kham Pur, West Patel Nagar, New Delhi110008.

The sample consisted of 12x189 Sh. Mukesh Kumar vs Food Safety Officer on 4 September, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198673385/
1 gm. sealed plastic pouches of Pan Masala (Ready for Sale), which was originally in sealed condition having declaration on it.

One counterpart of the sample was sent by the FSO to Food Analyst, Delhi situated at Lawrence Road Industrial Area.
3.
The Food Analyst vide Report No. FSS/481/2016 dated 22.10.2016 reported the sample to be misbranded on two counts.

First, violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2.5(ii)(b) of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011 read with Regulation No. 3.1.10(i) of the Mukesh Kumar & Anr. Vs. FSO Food Safety and Standards (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Regulations, 2011, as declaration of the flavouring agent was not written on the package,
as per the Regulations.

sentences.text: Secondly, violation of Regulation No. 2.2.2(10) of the FSS (Packaging and Labelling) Regulations, 2011, as the word "within" was printed on the package in the statement with respect to Best Before Date.
It has been stated that the appellants filed the reply, however, the same was not considered by the Ld. Adjudicating Officer in judicial manner.
4. Considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, the Ld. Adjudicating Officer imposed cumulative penalty of Rs.50,000/ collectively upon the appellants u/s 52 of the FSS Act, 2006.

5. Sh. Kundan Lal, Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has submitted that the Ld. AO/ADM has rightly imposed the penalties upon the appellants because the sample of the article was found to be misbranded, as in the lebel of the sample, relevant Regulations were not complied with.

Ld. Chief PP for the respondent has also filed brief written submissions, wherein he has relied upon Regulation No. 2.2.2.5(ii)(b) of the Food Safety and Standards (Packaging & Labelling), Regulations,
2011, which deals with the declaration regarding food additives.

Regulations, 2011 of the FSS Act, 2006.

sentences.text: 6. Per contra, Sh. R.K. Ahuja, Ld.

Counsel for the appellants has submitted that the complaint was filed against the nominee of the company and the company only on the basis of label declaration and that the invoice was not issued by the FBO i.e. Sh. Pawan Kumar Madan, M/s Pawan Store from where the sample of 'Pan Masala' was taken by the FSO.
It has further been submitted that the FBO failed to produce any invoice of purchase of the sample.

It has further been submitted that there is no evidence on the record that the appellant company has actually manufactured and supplied the article to the FBO and, therefore, the Ld. AO/ADM should not have imposed penalty upon the appellants/company.
It has further been submitted that the genuineness of label cannot be presumed merely on the basis of label declaration and rather the invoice of purchase is required.
It has further been submitted that the Ld. AO/ADM has passed the order without considering and examining various other points raised by the appellants.
It has further been submitted that the sample has not been tested in a valid laboratory.

Ld. Counsel for the Mukesh Kumar & Anr. Vs. FSO appellants has relied upon the following judgments:
i. Kishore Kumar Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2009 (2) FAC 333;

In Shyam Lal (Supra), it was inter alia held as under:
"It seems to us clear that the true rule of construction of a penal statute is that where the legislature evinces its intention to modify the law, in favour of the accused so as to reduce the rigour of the law in the light of past experience and changed social conditions so long as prosecution of the accused has not concluded by a judgment of conviction, the proceedings against him are regarded as inchoate and the law applicable to him would be the law as amended by the legislature.

"Reference was also made by their Lordships to certain observations appearing in Rattan Lal v. The State of Punjab, AIR 1965 SC 444, wherein it was held that an ex post facto law which only modifies the rigour of a criminal law would operate retrospectively.

Mr. B.T. Singh, Ld. Counsel representing the State did not cite any authority to the contrary and these authorities referred to above unmistakably help the petitioners."
10.

In respect of violation regarding "within", reliance has been placed on Ram Babu Rastogi (Supra), wherein it was inter alia held as under:
"13.
The allegations of misbranding against the petitioners were that the sample product declared the label as "Best before within 6 months from date of packaging".

The only grievance of the Department was that the word "within" which stood omitted after 01.09.2001 was added by the petitioners in the label and that made the same as misbranded because of clear violation of Rule 32(i).
Had the grievance been that there was no declaration at all, the things would Mukesh Kumar & Anr. Vs. FSO have to be viewed differently with different observations.

The objective of the declaration of the label was that the purchaser should know at the time of purchase,
as to whether the article, which is purchased was capable of being used and till what time.

14. The actual label found at the sample article i.e. "Best before within 6 months from date of packaging" conveyed much more than which was required to be conveyed to the purchasers about the genuineness of the product.
Mere use of word "within" as a surplusage would not bring the petitioners under the penal provisions of the Act.
By any means, the purchasers could not be said to have been deceived or misled as regards the character, quantity, quality or date of manufacture and the limit of use of the product.

15. In the case of Nehrudasan Vs. Food Inspector, Madurai Corporation, Madurai,
2010(1) FAC 49, the Madras High Court in somewhat similar case of prosecution based on the contravention of Rule 32 of the Act referred to a decision of the same High Court in A. Rajasingh & Ors. Vs. The Food Inspector, 2008(1) FAC 172 wherein it was held as under:

16.

In another case titled T. Prabhu & Another Vs. The State, 2007(1) FAC 314 also, the Madras High Court held that though the word "within" stands omitted after 01.09.2011, but by merely adding such word, the customers could not be said to have been misled or misdirected as there was no difference otherwise in the meaning conveyed.

In another case titled Hindustan Lever Limited and Others Vs. Food Inspector, 2007(1) FAC 299, the Madras High Court held similar view on the label which contained the similar word as in the instant case i.e. "best before within 6 months from date of packaging".
11.

sentences.text: It has been brought on the record that fresh Regulations came into effect in 2020 and the same has been duly notified.
The benefit of such Regulations cannot be denied to the appellants.

The other violation as alleged against the appellants also seems to be squarely covered in the judgment of Ram Babu Rastogi (Supra).
12.
It is also pertinent to mention here that there is nothing on the record to connect the appellants with the sample seized by the Food Inspector.

In Bhola Ram (Supra), it was inter alia held as under:
"3. In the absence of a bill, cash memorandum or invoice in respect of the sale of any article of food given by a manufacturer or distributor or a dealer to a vendor, there could arise no presumption on the mere label or wrapper that the person purported to Mukesh Kumar & Anr. Vs. FSO be the manufacturer, distributor or dealer thereof is in fact such manufacturer, distributor or dealer.
The bare word of the vendor in that regard would not be enough.
There had to be something more to it.

On the file,
there is no bill, cash memorandum or invoice in respect of the article of food sold.

Thus no occasion for the present has arisen to employ even the provisions of Section 20A of the Act in impleading the Petitioner as an accused in the case....."
13.
In view of the discussions made hereinabove, the appeal is allowed.
The FDR for an amount of Rs.50,000/, furnished by Appellant No. 2, be released against proper receipt.
14. Copy of the judgment be sent to the Ld. Trial Court, and thereafter the appeal file be consigned to Record Room.
